title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: declarative agents ground answers in scanned PDFs from SharePoint
summary: The control paths and commands are supported, and the roadmap dates and scope match. Hold for the claim that no further prerequisites are stated: Microsoft documents that Restricted SharePoint Search prevents using SharePoint knowledge. The page also overstates what is known about previously unreadable scans and overlooks the roadmap's reliability statement.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: SharePoint grounding is bounded by the asking user's existing content access.

claims.claim: The feature operates under the asking user's identity rather than a separate agent account.
claims.quote: Searched: 'declarative agents SharePoint knowledge retrieval signed in user identity permissions separate agent account'; read knowledge sources and TypeSpec. They establish user-bounded retrieval, not a processing account. Authentication details found concern Foundry, not this feature.
claims.fix: Replace 'so access follows the asking user's identity and licence rather than a separate agent account' with 'and SharePoint grounding is limited to content that user can access'.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not describe a separate identity specifically for scanned-content processing in this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: 'declarative agent scanned PDF grounding processing identity accuracy quality older agents SharePoint restricted content discovery specific URL'; read knowledge sources, TypeSpec and Agent Builder. No scan-processing identity description found.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes grounding answers, not adding new actions.
claims.quote: Any newly created Declarative Agents can now reliably ground answers in scanned PDFs and image-based documents referenced from SharePoint

claims.claim: Agents could not use scanned documents before this change, so permission problems never mattered for those unreadable files.
claims.quote: Searched: '"declarative agents" "scanned"' and '"declarative agents" "PDF" disable image understanding pricing existing agents'; read roadmap and release notes. The record says 'previously hard to use', not unusable; no universal prior inability established.
claims.fix: Replace 'permissions problems that never mattered for unreadable files start to matter' with 'existing permission problems can become more visible'. Replace 'Scanned documents that agents could not use before become usable as answer sources' with 'Scanned documents described by the roadmap as previously hard to use become more usable as answer sources'.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center path to block an agent is Agents > All agents > agent > Block.
claims.quote:
Select Agents > All agents.
In the All agents page, select an agent from the list of agents.
In the agent details pane that opens, immediately under the agent's name, select Block or Unblock.

claims.claim: POST /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a Copilot package.
claims.quote:
Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: The Graph block call is a beta API.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: Access to the Graph Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.claim: The Graph block call takes no request body.
claims.quote: Don't supply a request body for this method.

claims.claim: The admin center Block action restricts the selected agent across the organisation.
claims.quote: Block or unblock agents for the entire organization by using the same controls that work for any other app in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Blocking Agent Builder or Copilot Studio agents affects Copilot and other host products.
claims.quote: Blocking or unblocking an agent that you created by using Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder and Microsoft Copilot Studio affects its availability and functionality in Microsoft Copilot. It also affects availability and functionality in other host products

claims.claim: Blocking SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry agents affects only Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: However, blocking an agent that you created by using SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry only impacts its availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: The SharePoint admin center path is Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote:
In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites.
Select the site you want to configure.
Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery for a site.

Enable Restricted Content Discovery for a site
Use PowerShell

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery does not change existing permissions.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't change existing permissions. Users who already have access to content can continue to access that content directly.
